newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU Court upholds $95 mln fine against Tetra Pak.
newsitem.headline: EU Court upholds $95 mln fine against Tetra Pak.

text.p: The European Court of Justice rejected on Thursday an appeal by Swedish carton marker Tetra Pak against a 75-million-European currency unit ($95.5 million) fine imposed by the European Commission.

The Commission fined Tetra Pak in July 1991 after concluding that the company had broken European Union competition rules by "bullying" rivals and slashing prices to control the European market for over a decade.
The court "dismisses the apppeal," the ruling said, condemning Tetra Pak to pay the costs involved in the legal action.
The ruling follows a 1994 judgment by the European Court of First Instance, the EU's lower court, which upheld the Commission's decision.
On Thursday, the court confirmed the judgment and in particular rejected the claim that the fine should at least be reduced.

Tetra Pak International SA, a Swiss-registered company originally from Sweden which coordinates the policy of a group of companies, argued that the fine should have been lower because of the Commission's unprecedented application of methods and competition rules to the sector.

The company, which specialises in equipment for packaging liquid or semi-liquid food products in cartons, argued that article 86 of the EU treaty -- which bans abuse of dominant position -- was not applicable to the sector.

"Even if in some respects defining the relevant product markets and the scope of article 86 may have been a matter of some complexity, Tetra Pak could not have been unaware, given its quasi-monoply on the aseptic (packaging) markets and its leading position on the non-aseptic markets, that the practices in issue contravened the rules in the treaty", the court said in its judgement.
